Long Post Alert!

Women's Hospital "Room Harmony" has been etched in my memory as it  was my home for two and a half months.
I had a complicated pregnancy and was advised completed bed rest and was admitted under Dr. Gayatri Rao's guidance who turned my hope into reality. She is the sweetest soul who would brighten my dark days with her encouraging words and smile.
On April 2nd, I delivered a premature baby boy after the long tiring journey.
I would also like to thank the nurses who had made my stay homely with utmost care and positivity. They were nice to me and somehow became my friends by the time I was leaving.
A big shoutout to sisters - Vidya, Hema, Trishala, Smita, Mayuri, Namrata, Alpa, Yashika, Sunita and I might have missed few other names but I am equally grateful to each.

Not only the nurses even the maushis were accomodating everytime I had to use the loo as I was on complete bed rest.

Last but not the least, I would also love to mention few other doctors who helped me with the littlest difficulty, doubt, concern even during the middle of the night namely Dr. Dipali, Dr. Vijaya, Dr. Shalini, Dr. Surti and Dr. Dolly.

Dr. Dipali was very empathetic soul who would keep visiting my room and appreciating and encouraging me to overcome each day in the hospital. Dr. Vijaya would flawlessly put the IV drip's on me with most care and concern avoiding any chances of hurting me. Also, Dr. Manju sinha would keep visiting and advising me to read books for a positivity.

Another appreciation I would want to give the phlebotomist who would come for my blood tests and would tell me lovingly that I would be a good mom. I forgot her name but I hope you guys will find out who she is.

It was a tumultuous journey for both me and my husband, but the way Dr. Gayatri Rao made my pregnancy possible with her positive smile and golden words is beyond everything.

It was a long stay but it became bearable with each and every person mentioned above. Thank you guys, for helping me out during the most fragile yet memorable time of my life. I will always be indebted to this hospital.

The only drawback if I may mention are the charges of the hospital as it is located at the posh side of bandra khar. But, for middle class people like us the charges were indeed challenging.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We started treatment with this doctor after 4 years of marriage. We underwent around 3 months of infertility treatment and after consistent follow-ups, we finally conceived. Unfortunately, at around 1.5 months we came to know that the baby was not growing, and we had to go through a very difficult loss. After taking a short break, we were blessed to conceive naturally.

During the next pregnancy, we faced multiple complications including gestational diabetes, low placenta placement, and bleeding in the 5th month. Throughout this challenging journey, the doctor was knowledgeable, supportive, and gave us confidence. Our due date was in January, but towards the end of pregnancy, due to diabetes-related concerns, we were advised for an early C-section and were blessed with our baby girl on 30th December 2023.

Again, we got good news in 2025. This pregnancy was comparatively smoother, but because of our previous pregnancy history and diabetes concerns, a similar situation was created again even before 35 weeks, and we were advised to prepare for an early delivery. Thankfully, we were blessed with our second baby girl.

Overall, the doctor is friendly, experienced, and knowledgeable, and we are grateful for the care that helped us become parents of two beautiful daughters.

However, one area where we felt improvement is needed is communication during critical decisions. In both pregnancies, the recommendation for C-section came in a very urgent and stressful manner, which left us feeling panicked and with very little time to fully understand, discuss, or mentally prepare for such a major decision. As patients, especially during emotional moments, clearer explanation and more time for discussion would have helped us feel more involved and reassured.

Still, we sincerely appreciate the doctor’s efforts and care throughout our journey and wish the team all the best.

A special thanks to the nursing and support staff, especially Aly, Hema, Sushma, and all the mavashies, for their care, kindness, and support during difficult and emotional moments. Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.

Not every normal delivery progresses smoothly till the end. In some cases, labour advances well but the baby does not deliver despite good contractions. When the cervix is fully open and the baby’s head is already low, vacuum assisted delivery may be used to help complete the birth safely. This is a form of assisted delivery used only under specific conditions.

During vacuum delivery, a suction cup is attached to the baby’s head and gentle assistance is given while the mother pushes with contractions. This helps reduce prolonged strain during the second stage of labour and allows timely delivery when support is needed.

At Pradnya Maternity IVF and Multispeciality Hospital in Mulund, Dr Pradnya Randive manages labour and delivery with careful assessment at every stage. The focus is on safe normal delivery, early identification of delivery delays, and using assisted methods only when they are medically appropriate for the mother and baby.

Heavy Periods & Painful Periods Should Not Be Ignored

Many women experience heavy bleeding during periods, severe cramps, or both, and assume it is normal. However, when periods last more than 7 days, involve passing large clots, or require frequent pad changes, this condition is called menorrhagia. When periods are extremely painful and interfere with daily activities, it is known as dysmenorrhea.

According to Dr. Pradnya Randive, Obstetrician Gynaecologist and Fertility Specialist at Pradnya Maternity IVF & Multispeciality Hospital, Mulund, these symptoms often have underlying medical causes such as fibroids, endometriosis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), or thyroid-related problems. Ignoring them can lead to anaemia, fertility issues, and long-term health complications.

Early consultation with a gynaecologist helps identify the cause through basic evaluations such as blood tests and pelvic sonography, allowing timely and effective treatment. Not all heavy or painful periods require surgery, but they do require proper medical assessment.

At Pradnya Maternity IVF & Multispeciality Hospital, women receive personalised care for menstrual problems, pregnancy, and normal delivery, with a focus on accurate diagnosis and safe treatment.

If you are facing heavy bleeding, painful periods, or irregular cycles, consult a gynaecologist early and avoid self-medication.

featured_reviews.name: Gurprit Gill
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am deeply disappointed and frustrated by my experience at this fertility clinic.

I first visited the clinic in February 2026 based on a recommendation from a close friend. After witnessing everything we have endured over the past several months, that friend now regrets recommending the clinic in the first place.

From the outset, we made it absolutely clear that our goal was to proceed with IVF treatment. Initial test results were described as positive, yet we were told that a cyst needed to be removed before moving forward. Trusting the medical advice provided, we underwent surgery and completed a full course of costly medications. However, instead of progressing toward IVF as expected, we were placed on additional medications for nearly two more months with little to no explanation of how this was advancing our treatment plan.

By May, after repeatedly requesting clarity and asking why IVF had still not begun, estrogen tablets and other hormone medications were prescribed. A Serum E2 test was then performed while these medications were being taken. We were informed that the E2 level was high and were instructed to continue medication for another month. The exact same pattern occurred again during the June cycle: hormone medications continued, another E2 test was conducted, the result was again described as high, and treatment was postponed yet another time with more medications prescribed.

What is most troubling is the persistent lack of transparency and communication. Critical information is rarely explained clearly during consultations. Instead, patients are expected to return for multiple appointments to obtain answers that should have been provided openly and proactively. Despite significant waiting times at each visit, straightforward explanations and clear guidance remain difficult to obtain.

From February through the end of June, five valuable months passed without any meaningful progress toward the IVF treatment we originally sought. During that time, we experienced a continuous cycle of delays, repeated testing, additional medications, and postponed treatment milestones. On one occasion, treatment was delayed even further because the doctor was unavailable.

Fertility treatment is one of the most emotionally, physically, and financially challenging journeys a person can undertake. Patients place enormous trust in their healthcare providers and deserve honesty, transparency, timely communication, and a clearly defined treatment strategy. Unfortunately, our experience fell far short of those expectations. We invested months of time, significant financial resources, and considerable emotional energy into this process, yet received very little clarity regarding our actual progress toward IVF.

Based on our experience, I strongly encourage prospective patients to ask detailed questions, insist on clear explanations for every delay or change in treatment, and seriously consider obtaining a second opinion before committing to a long-term treatment plan at this clinic.

From the doctors and nurses to the housekeeping staff , room service and all the attendants everyone played a vital role in making our journey comfortable and reassuring. The nurses took such gentle care of my newborn, helping with feeding and ensuring my wife and baby both are always safe, warm and well looked after.  Most importantly, we truly appreciate the way entire team cared for my wife as new mother. The kindness , patience, responsiveness and constant encouragement helped my wife to recover with confidence and peace of mind. Thank you to the entire fortis maternity ward team for your dedication, compassion and hard work. We highly recommend Fortis Nest for maternity and related treatment.

featured_reviews.name: PSM
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had our second baby at Fortis Hospital Mulund's NEST department.

No matter how much you plan, some things are just out of your control - While we hoped for a normal delivery, we ended up needing a C-section.

The medical care was excellent and we felt completely safe.

Dr. Sangeeta Raodeo was fantastic - always calm, clear with her explanations, and available whenever we called during pregnancy. She guided us through everything and gave us confidence during delivery.

The hospital staff was genuinely helpful. The nurses (especially the night shift), cleaning crew, food team, and even security on a few occasions helped us with our requests. The hospital itself was clean and well-organized.

However, the billing department on the 9th floor was a nightmare. The staff seemed completely unprofessional and deliberately made patients wait unnecessarily for running bills. On discharge day, they basically harass you and will overcharge by at least 10%-15% if you're not extremely vigilant. The accounts team won't listen to complaints or help resolve issues.

Thankfully, Dr. Raodeo stepped in to help us sort out the billing mess - she's truly a gem! We were eventually able to meet the billing head directly to resolve things.

Once again, special thanks to Dr. Sangeeta Raodeo, and the NEST team for excellent medical care. Just be very careful with billing.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavik Kothari
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a truly beautiful experience at Fortis Hospital Mulund (Nest Maternity Department) for the delivery of our baby boy.
A heartfelt thank you to Dr. Atul Ganatra for making our entire 9-month journey smooth and stress-free. His guidance, every advice, and friendly nature gave us a lot of confidence and comfort throughout the pregnancy. We are extremely grateful for his support and care.
Special thanks to Dr. Prachi for her constant care and always welcoming us with a smile.
We would also like to thank Sister Sakshi and her entire nursing team for taking such great care of my wife and baby round the clock during our stay at Nest. Their dedication, support, and attention made us feel safe and cared for at all times.
Thank you to everyone at Fortis Nest for making this journey so memorable and special.
